messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,
The source code is all available on github. I made changes to the ectoR_devel and ectotherm functions. For ectoR_devel, the change is relatively simple – I just added a new variable ‘Q_act’, which is how many extra watts the animal produces due to flight (or some other activity). You can calculate this however you like, outside of running ectoR_devel, and it is just added on to the resting metabolic rate. Note also I’ve added the fourth parameter of the Andrews and Pough 1985 metabolic rate vs. Tb and body mass to both ectoR_devel and ectotherm.

For the ectotherm model, the relevant parameters are:
flyer = 0, Does the animal fly? 1=yes, 0=no
flymetab = 0, metabolic cost of flight, W
flyhigh = 0, Does the animal fly at ref height? 1=yes, 0=no
flyspeed = 5, flight speed (m/s)

It all gets activated if flyer = 1. Then, the program will add the flymetab value to the base metabolic rate before calculating body temperature so pre-warming of the flight muscles can happen to see if the animal can take off. If not, it turns the excess heat production off and continues as normal, not trying to fly. If it can take off, then it will try solving the heat budget in the flight environment, which is affected by ‘flyhigh’ and ‘flyspeed’. The ‘flyspeed’ parameter is the new wind speed (it takes the maximum of this value and the wind speed at the height the animal is flying). The ‘flyhigh’ parameter makes the animal fly at the ‘reference height’ if 1, and at the local height if 0.
All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: timeinterval issue over New Years
messages.body_plain:
Hi Josh,

I see you are running simulations in Australia. That micro_global function uses a monthly climate dataset and splines the monthly data to daily when timeinterval = 365. The jump you see is to do with the spline. I suggest you instead use the new micro_silo function, which uses historical gridded data for Australia. You could do the actual days you have data for that way. Note you just have to put your email address in the micro_silo function as one of the input arguments, which is required to access the SILO data <https://www.longpaddock.qld.gov.au/silo/>.

Note that the micro_global function will run each day three times to get a 'steady periodic' of soil temperatures (and snow/soil moisture) from the initial conditions, unless timeinterval = 365 in which case it uses the soil temperatures (and snow/soil moisture) of midnight on the previous day as the initial conditions for the next day. So, although you saw a jump in the air temps due to the spline, you should see a smooth transition in soil temps etc. (and local-height air temp if you were modelling air temperatures close to the ground).

I see you have the height of the animal set to 1.4 m and you changed the reference height to 1.4 m as well. Definitely don't do the latter. The Refhyt parameter is the height of your weather data observations. It should stay at the default value (1.2 m for micro_global).

All the best,
Mike

The error indicates that it can't find the fortran compiler, so the problem is with how you're installing fortran " /opt/gfortran/bin/gfortran: No such file or directory"
Googling that error I got to this page <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69639782/installing-gfortran-on-macbook-with-apple-m1-chip-for-use-in-r> which you can have a look at and try out or see if you can find other solutions.

Dear Mac users,
If you've had trouble compilling NicheMapR, make sure you've got the right version of R for your chip (Intel vs am64 silicon) - R will still run if it's the wrong version but won't compile Fortran properly. Also, get the correct version of gfortran from here <https://mac.r-project.org/tools/>
All the best,
Mike

And Dan Noble has made these notes for OSX (thanks Dan)

# 1. Install gfortran using homebrew in the terminal/bash window
   brew install gcc
# 2. Take note of the path to gfortran. You'll need this for later
    which gfortran

# 3. In home directory of terminal create a Makevars file
   mkdir ~/.R
   touch ~/.R/Makevars
   open  ~/.R/Makevars

# 4. Add the following to the Makevars file. Note that you need to make sure your version of fortran is correct and replace 124.2.0_1 with your version. You can find version in terminal by typing `gfortran --version`. In addition you need to replace the path to gfortran with the path you found in step 2.
    FC = /opt/homebrew/Cellar/gcc/14.2.0_1/bin/gfortran
   F77 = /opt/homebrew/Cellar/gcc/14.2.0_1/bin/gfortran
 FLIBS = -L/opt/homebrew/Cellar/gcc/14.2.0_1/lib/gcc/11

#5. Restart R and try to install the package again via devtools. It should now work.
